frontier.hypothesis: Stopping loop.c's move_movables from hoisting insn 327, `(set (reg:SI 140) (symbol_ref/v:SI ("D_800A9A24")))`, out of the inner loop body is SUFFICIENT to close this axis — s6 measured or derived every step downstream of it.
frontier.mechanism: A block-local 140 receives the same nsugg=1 $a1 suggestion `off` has (block_alloc scans all register operands of insn 229), ties `off` on qty_sugg_compare's first key, and wins the priority key 60000 vs 20000 because its live range would be 2 index units against `off`'s measured 6 at the same loop-depth-weighted refs=6. It takes $a1; `off` then fails the just_try_suggested pass and the plain pass hands it $v0 (first free in REG_ALLOC_ORDER given used={0,1,4,5,26..67}).
frontier.next_probe: Get move_movables' per-movable log for this loop. cc1's loop dump is the -dL stream, which tools/grinder/dump.ps1 does not request; invoke the existing cc1 binary directly with the loop dump enabled from a scratch script (pattern: tmp/grind/func_80041BF4/s6/rtlord.sh) — do NOT edit anything under tools/. Read the `savings N` line for regno 140, then identify which of m->savings / m->lifetime / already_moved / m->forces would have to differ for the gate at loop.c:1631 to fail, and ask whether any honest C form changes that field. s5 already closed the naming route (a C name lengthens the live range to whole-function and costs 5 insns via $s8 eviction), so a declaration is not the answer.

frontier.hypothesis: If the loop.c hoist is not C-reachable without an opaque-arithmetic construct, the register-allocation axis for this function is exhausted and the residual must be attacked from a different direction (rederive / synthesis) rather than with more allocation work.
frontier.mechanism: s3 closed declaration order (15 permutations, 2 chassis) and inner-body expression shape (33 spellings); s4/s5 closed permuter (60k+ iterations, 3 chassis) and the naming routes; s6 closed the live-range-conflict route and the operand-order route. The hoist itself is the only untried lever left inside the allocator.
frontier.next_probe: Before spending another allocation session, re-derive the function body from target's asm independently of the current chassis — in particular test whether the original source computed the LoadImage source address from a different expression tree (e.g. an index into an array of 32-byte elements) that never produces a bare `(set reg (symbol_ref))` inside the loop at all.
